items.title: Behind the growing power of No Surprises Act arbitrators - Modern Healthcare
items.reason: The article directly addresses the Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process under the No Surprises Act, specifically examining the role and expanding influence of arbitrators who adjudicate these disputes.
items.summary: Modern Healthcare reports on the increasing authority and impact of arbitrators administering the No Surprises Act's Independent Dispute Resolution process. The article examines how IDR arbitrators are becoming more powerful players in resolving out-of-network billing disputes between payers and providers. This development affects revenue-cycle teams by influencing how balance-billing disputes are resolved and potentially setting precedents that shape future claim denials and payment determinations under the No Surprises Act framework.

items.title: Providers sue Cigna over alleged $12.8 million addiction claims shortfall - Insurance Business
items.reason: This is a provider lawsuit against a major payer (Cigna) alleging claims-denial/underpayment on a specific dollar amount, which directly falls within the payer litigation category of the topic definition.
items.summary: Providers have filed a lawsuit against Cigna alleging the payer underpaid addiction treatment claims by $12.8 million. The suit challenges Cigna's handling of claims related to substance-use disorder services, representing a claims-denial and potential downcoding dispute between providers and the insurer. This case is relevant to revenue-cycle teams as it involves substantive questions about how a major national payer processes and reimburses claims in a high-stakes clinical category, with potential implications for similar claims across provider networks.

items.title: Health insurer Anthem targeted in lawsuit over air ambulance claims - Indianapolis Business Journal
items.reason: This is a lawsuit directly targeting Anthem (Elevance), a major payer, over claims handling practices (air ambulance claim denials/delays), which falls squarely within payer litigation and enforcement scope.
items.summary: Anthem, a major health insurer, is facing a lawsuit related to its handling of air ambulance claims, according to reporting by the Indianapolis Business Journal. The suit alleges improper claims management practices by the payer. This litigation is relevant to revenue-cycle teams as it involves potential claims-denial or claims-processing disputes with a major national payer, which could affect provider reimbursement and payment timelines for emergency transport services covered under Anthem plans.

items.title: DOL Backs Aramark Bid To Avoid Aetna ERISA Suit Arbitration - Law360
items.reason: This item involves regulatory/enforcement action by the DOL and an ERISA litigation matter involving a major payer (Aetna), which directly matches the topic definition's scope of payer litigation and regulatory enforcement.
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Labor has backed Aramark's position in an ERISA dispute with Aetna, supporting the company's bid to avoid arbitration of the suit. The DOL's backing represents a regulatory intervention in a fiduciary/ERISA claim involving the major health insurer Aetna. This development affects companies facing ERISA litigation with payers and illustrates how DOL positions can influence arbitration disputes in healthcare benefits contexts. The outcome may impact how similar fund-diversion or fiduciary claims proceed against insurers.
